findings.finding: The first nonblank block precedes every chapter. An ordinary chapter-context assignment would drop it, invent a chapter or mix Quranic quotations into a numbered hadith. An explicit pinned book-introduction declaration now preserves it separately.

The selected digital paragraph stops after the short amount-of-a-sa transmission. Both inspected Arabic prints include a further Abu Abdullah note about Ibn Uyaynah later relating via Ibn Abbas from Maymunah, followed by a preference for Abu Nuaym’s transmission. The selected digital paragraph does not contain that final note. Bewley 250 also includes it; the checked EPUB 1.5.253 contains the short report body without either closing note.
findings.separateVariant: The historical print places the short amount-of-a-sa note after the earlier Aisha report and does not repeat it after this account. The modern print includes it in both locations. The selected digital repetition therefore has support in the inspected modern print; it must not be removed merely because it resembles an earlier note.
findings.nextDecision: The first batch retains the original paragraph and supplies the final note as a separately labelled modern-print block, with both readings and English coverage. Independent review remains pending.

findings.finding: Bewley’s online introduction labels the second quotation 4:42; the inspected modern Arabic print labels it 4:43. Preserve the comparison as evidence but do not import its verse number without checking the Quranic reference.
